html:
The Aghlabids were a dynasty of emirs who ruled Ifriqiya, roughly today's Tunisia and eastern Algeria, from 800 to 909, nominally for the Abbasid caliphs in Baghdad.

From Kairouan they built a strong state. They rebuilt the Great Mosque of Kairouan largely in the form it has today, dug great water reservoirs, and fortified the coast with ribats, such as the one at Sousse. Kairouan became a centre of Maliki Sunni law.

In 827 they sent a fleet to Sicily, beginning the Arab conquest of the island (Emirate of Sicily), and raided Italy as far as Rome. In 909 they were overthrown by Berber followers of the Fatimid movement, who set up the Fatimid Caliphate at Mahdia.
sum: The Aghlabids were a dynasty of emirs who ruled Ifriqiya, roughly today's Tunisia and eastern Algeria, from 800 to 909, nominally for the Abbasid caliphs in Baghdad.
